title: Fault-tolerant execution of error-corrected quantum algorithms
topic: Quantum hardware / fault-tolerant quantum computation / Quantinuum Helios
summary: First end-to-end demonstration of fault-tolerant execution of complete quantum algorithms (QAOA and HHL) on Quantinuum H2 and Helios processors using the [[7,1,3]] Steane code. QAOA circuits up to 12 logical (97 physical) qubits with 2132 physical 2-qubit gates still show better-than-random performance. Demonstrates FT logical T-gate implementation, active QEC cycles, and repeat-until-success state preparation on live hardware.
key_findings: End-to-end FT execution of QAOA (5-8 logical qubits) and HHL on Quantinuum H2 and Helios
12 logical (97 physical) qubits with 2132 physical 2-qubit gates: better-than-random performance achieved
Steane [[7,1,3]] code used throughout; increasing T-gate count and QAOA layers still improves performance
Active QEC cycles and repeat-until-success state prep demonstrated as critical capabilities
Helios enables higher qubit counts than H2 for the same logical circuit
project_relevance: WATCH. Confirms Helios is operational for algorithmic use (not just error correction benchmarks). The 2132 physical 2-qubit gate budget with 97 physical qubits is directly relevant to our planned MERA circuit: our 32q/3L design has 57 CX gates (well within this budget). The demonstrated tolerance for deep circuits with QEC suggests our 0.9% error budget estimate is conservative. Does not change our circuit design but strengthens the hardware access case.
competition_assessment: Not competing. Different application domain (optimization/linear algebra vs holographic physics). Strengthens hardware access case.
